jobDescription: A hotel group with mid-market and budget brands across 70 properties is expanding its revenue management analytics. The data scientist builds room-demand forecasts and price-elasticity models, presents pricing recommendations to general managers and the commercial director, keeps the data pipeline from the property management system healthy, evaluates pricing tests and helps revenue managers make use of the pricing dashboard. Recommendations are discussed at a monthly commercial review, and the group expects every adopted or rejected recommendation to be minuted with the reason.
requirements: Builds room-demand forecasts and price-elasticity models.
Presents pricing recommendations to general managers and the commercial director and records the decisions taken.
Maintains the data pipeline from the property management system.
Evaluates pricing tests against control hotels.
Trains revenue managers in using the pricing dashboard.

evidence.text: Revenue management data scientist at Brightwater Hotels (42 mid-market hotels), March 2022 to present, building nightly room-demand forecasts and price-elasticity estimates by hotel and booking window.

Presented the monthly pricing recommendations at the commercial review attended by the commercial director and the regional general managers, and kept the action log showing which recommendations were adopted.
Maintained the daily extract from the property management system into the warehouse, with row-count and late-arrival checks that alert the data engineering rota.
Evaluated the 2023 weekend minimum-stay test against six matched control hotels using a difference-in-differences comparison over twelve weeks.
Produced a four-page guide to the pricing dashboard for revenue managers, explaining the forecast bands and the recommended-rate column, and posted it on the commercial team's intranet page.

Work sample: the September 2023 commercial review pack, with the candidate's three pricing recommendations and the elasticity estimates behind each, and the minutes recording that the commercial director adopted two and deferred the third until the minimum-stay test had finished.
Reference check summary: the commercial director confirmed in writing that the candidate presented at the monthly commercial review throughout 2023 and 2024 and maintained its action log.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate would need to give one month's notice and is open to travelling to the regional hotels two days a month.

propositions.text: The candidate presented monthly pricing recommendations at the commercial review and kept the action log; in September 2023 the commercial director adopted two of the three recommendations and deferred the third.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the presentations, the work sample contains the September 2023 pack and minutes, and the reference confirms the role at the review.

propositions.text: The candidate evaluated the 2023 weekend minimum-stay test against six matched control hotels using difference-in-differences.
propositions.rationale: The resume entry describes the test design directly.

propositions.text: The candidate maintained the daily extract from the property management system with row-count and late-arrival checks.
propositions.rationale: The resume entry describes the pipeline and its checks.

gold.expectedGap: A written dashboard guide is described, but no training sessions for revenue managers are documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the commercial review record, including the deferred recommendation, as supported evidence; do not attribute revenue outcomes to the adopted recommendations.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate trained revenue managers on the pricing dashboard beyond the written guide, and how many sessions were run.
